title: A Bayesian framework for longitudinal EHR and genetic discovery.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo API for record 20802505: access_right is 'restricted', resource type 'software', no public file list returned. GitHub repo surbut/aladynoulli2 full tree (104 entries): only five small tabular files, all summary outputs (polygenic-score-to-signature association tables of about 100 KB, and three-kilobyte model comparison tables under docs/reparam); no per-patient data.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Cohort sizes (total n > 683,000 across UK Biobank, Mass General Brigham and All of Us), 348 diseases, 21 signatures, 151 GWAS (genome-wide association study) loci, and the statement that individual-level data need a formal application or request from each biobank.

a1_downloadable.note: Checked: the per-patient diagnosis histories and genotypes sit in UK Biobank, MGB (Mass General Brigham) Biobank and All of Us, all of which need an access application. The Zenodo archive is marked 'restricted', and GitHub holds only small summary tables.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not reachable. The public files are model outputs (signature associations), not measured outcomes; disease onset labels exist only in the controlled biobank records.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs (per-patient ICD-10 diagnosis codes mapped to PheCodes, plus polygenic scores) are not public.

a5_enough_rows.note: The paper says >683,000 patients, but none are downloadable; the public GitHub tables are small summary files whose row counts I did not count.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not assessable; biobank-scale data would need a secure research environment anyway.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot compare; no individual-level file is accessible.

a8_label_provenance.note: The only public tables are outputs of the ALADYNOULLI model itself (signature loadings vs polygenic scores), so modelling them would mean learning from another model's predictions.

existing_models.name: ALADYNOULLI (this paper; Bayesian generative model of disease histories)
existing_models.score_and_split: Paper reports it beats the PCE (Pooled Cohort Equations), PREVENT and Gail risk scores at 1-year and 10-year horizons in three biobanks; code on GitHub under the MGB Source Available License; fitted weights not checked.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not extracted; evaluation stopped at Part A.

existing_models.name: Delphi-2M (code-level generative model of disease trajectories, named in this paper)
existing_models.score_and_split: Used in the paper as a comparison model; I did not retrieve its own paper.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim possible without the controlled biobank data.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a patient's past diagnoses, age and inherited genetic risk to predict which diseases they will develop next.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-patient time-stamped diagnosis histories plus polygenic risk scores from three biobanks (paper reports >683,000 patients; none publicly downloadable).
plain_idea.predict: Future disease onset (from hospital diagnosis codes) at 1-year and 10-year horizons, recorded in the biobank health records.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Clinicians and risk-score developers could flag high-risk patients earlier, but the data needs biobank access applications.

ml_idea: Disease-trajectory prediction from health records and polygenic scores; not feasible because all individual-level data are controlled access (UK Biobank, MGB Biobank, All of Us).

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Zenodo access_right field ('restricted') and the data availability statement: done, project killed.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: all patient-level data are controlled access (UK Biobank application, MGB Biobank by request, All of Us workspace), the Zenodo archive is restricted, and GitHub holds only small model-output summary tables, which would also fail A8.
